description.value: An independent analysis examined relationships between peripheral stress markers and prefrontal fMRI responses to neutral-relaxing, alcohol, and stress cues in early-abstinent alcohol-dependent patients.

value: We hypothesized a link between central and peripheral dysfunction in AD

We hypothesized that elevated basal heart rate, neutral-relaxed state cort:ACTH ratio, and stress induced cort:ACTH ratio would be positively related to VmPFC and rACC activation in the neutral-relaxing condition.

We also hypothesized that these measures of HPA axis and autonomic dysfunction would be inversely correlated with VmPFC and rACC activation in response to stress and alcohol cues in early AD abstinence.

description.value: Observational analysis of early-abstinent alcohol-dependent patients during inpatient treatment, with fMRI and laboratory cue-exposure sessions and prospective follow-up.

spans.text: we performed an independent analysis on a subgroup of AD participants

description.value: Participants listened to and imagined a personalized neutral, relaxing event. In the laboratory it was presented as a 5-minute audiotaped script; in fMRI it was a 2-minute script preceded by a quiet baseline and followed by recovery. It served as an active control condition and was intended not to increase alcohol craving.
